title: Why must Thunderbird have a 'Default' email account?
creator: DesertOutlaw1
content:
Example why question is being asked:

Three separate GMX email accounts, each with its own unique password, and NOW Application-specific password for Thunderbird. Aliases are not used or desired. Three different separate accounts that should each have its own outgoing server.

Worked fine until updates to Thunderbird and changes to the GMX server, and Application-specific passwords became a requirement to send and receive email.

Seems like updates to nearly every program and/or app that may be released with the intent to resolve an issue or include a new feature breaks something else. M$ is horrible with updates and labels nearly everything as a critical update so it gets pushed through even when updates are turned off or supposedly permanently disabled by a registry hack; Windows 11 being the absolute worse ever. Why I only have one computer with M$ while all the others are Linux. Problems all the time with M$ while Linux simply continues to work.

Regardless, can setup each GMX account but the default email account name must be used as the user name on the other two GMX accounts on the outgoing server in order to send email. Then the recipient sees the name for the default account rather than the name assigned to the other two accounts, and the Application-specific password for Thunderbird must be changed to that of the default. Then attempting to pull down email for the other two pop accounts comes to a halt, and email messages can only be viewed by going to the online account.

Two separate accounts for yahoo, two for gmail, and one for Charter work fine, each has its own name and outgoing server. Should be the same way for GMX but is not because Thunderbird requires one of the three GMX accounts is set to Default.

Appears by having a Default email account, users are not only restricted by the default account, but email that is sent is done so with he incorrect name, The purpose for three different emails is for email segregation and better management; personal correspondence, business related, and Internet stuff.

Instead of having a 'Default' email account, makes more sense to use a valid email to register Thunderbird after downloading and installing, and then using that email for Support, Boards, assistance, etc. The default email requirement causes too many frustrating unneeded issues that should not occur, along with wasted time, stress and grief. Computers were suppose to make our lives easier and allow us more time for the real world. Biggest lie told since the Bell Labs created the transistor.

creator: metinolmetin1
content:
Hem Windows masaüstü Thunderbird hem de Thunderbird Android mobil uygulamalarında, uzun süredir sorunsuz kullandığım kişisel e-posta hesabım (to******@live.com) ve test amacıyla yeni oluşturduğum e-posta hesabım (m******s@hotmail.com) üzerinde IMAP bağlantı hatası yaşanmaktadır.

Yaşanan Durum ve Denenen Adımlar: 1. Bu sorun daha önceden var olmayan, sonradan ortaya çıkan bir durumdur. Ayrıca istemcide tanımlı diğer e-posta hesaplarımda hiçbir problem yaşanmazken yalnızca bu iki Microsoft hesabında gözlemlenmektedir. 2. Otomatik ve manuel yapılandırmalarda IMAP (outlook.office365.com:993, SSL/TLS, OAuth 2.0) ve SMTP (smtp-mail.outlook.com:587, STARTTLS, OAuth 2.0) parametreleri eksiksiz girilmektedir. 3. Web tarayıcı yönlendirmesinde Microsoft 2 Adımlı Doğrulama (2FA) ve OAuth 2.0 oturumu başarıyla tamamlanıp izinler verilmektedir. 4. Giriş yapıldıktan hemen sonra istemci "Klasör listesi sunucudan alınamadı - User is authenticated but not connected" hatası döndürmekte ve senkronizasyon başarısız olmaktadır. 5. Sorunun ayarlarla ilgili olup olmadığını doğrulamak adına sıfır açılmış @hotmail.com hesabında IMAP/POP3 erişimleri aktif edilerek deneme yapılmış, aynı hata bu hesapta da tekrarlanmıştır. 6. Söz konusu iki hesap da Android için resmi Microsoft Outlook uygulamasına kurulduğunda ise hiçbir sorun yaşanmadan anında senkronize olmakta ve çalışmaktadır.

Sorunun Thunderbird OAuth 2.0 belirteç (token) işleme mekanizması ile Microsoft IMAP uç noktaları arasındaki el sıkışma uyumsuzluğundan kaynaklandığı değerlendirilmektedir. Konunun incelenmesini rica ederim.

title: Thunderbird keeps freezing after being left idle
creator: pavelconstantinov
content:
• Subject: Severe recurring UI freezes after upgrading Thunderbird from v114 to v150+ — application becomes unresponsive after being left idle**

Hello Thunderbird Support Team,

I'm experiencing a serious and persistent performance issue with Thunderbird that began immediately after upgrading from version 114 to version 150 in September 2026. The problem has continued through multiple subsequent updates and is now severely affecting my daily work.

I've been using Thunderbird for years, and it worked reliably before this major upgrade.

    • The problem**

Thunderbird launches normally and initially works perfectly. However, after I leave it open in the background while working in other applications, it frequently becomes completely unresponsive when I return to it.

Specifically:

- Thunderbird is initially fast and responsive after launching. - After approximately 5–10 minutes, or sometimes after a longer period of inactivity, it begins experiencing severe lag or freezes completely. - When I switch back to Thunderbird, the interface is often unresponsive for several minutes. - I often have to force-close the application through Windows because it becomes practically unusable. - Restarting Thunderbird temporarily restores normal performance, but the problem eventually returns, when it's left idle. - The issue occurs repeatedly throughout the day and makes it very difficult to use Thunderbird reliably.

Importantly, this is not simply slow startup performance. Thunderbird initially works perfectly, and the freezing develops after it has been running for a while, particularly when left in the background.

    • Version and environment**

- Operating system: Windows 11 Pro, 64-bit - Thunderbird version before the upgrade: 114 - Version initially upgraded to: 150 - Subsequently confirmed version: 156.0.1 (64-bit), on September 29, 2026 - Problem first appeared: September 2026 - Problem still present: October 22, 2026 - Current Thunderbird version: 158.0.1

    • Troubleshooting already performed**

1. **Global search indexing:** I noticed that Thunderbird's Activity Manager frequently displayed "Indexing messages." I suspected that indexing might be causing the problem.

2. **Disabled Global Search and Indexer (Gloda):** Unfortunately, this made no meaningful difference. Thunderbird continued freezing even with global indexing disabled.

3. **Multiple Thunderbird updates:** The application has been updated repeatedly since the initial upgrade, but the freezing has persisted.

4. **Restarting Thunderbird:** Temporarily resolves the problem, but only until Thunderbird has been running for some time.

    • Additional unusual behavior: Google OAuth authentication**

On at least two occasions, after force-closing an unresponsive Thunderbird process, Google Chrome unexpectedly opened a Google authorization page saying:

"Mozilla Thunderbird Email wants access to your Google Account."

The page also indicated that Thunderbird already had some access to the Google account.

After clicking "Continue," Chrome redirected to a localhost address (127.0.0.1 equivalent, using a dynamically assigned port), which failed with:

"ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED — localhost refused to connect."

I suspect this happens because Thunderbird is no longer running to receive the OAuth authorization callback.

I'm not sure whether the Google authorization issue is directly related to the freezes, but the repeated timing is suspicious and could indicate a background synchronization or authentication problem.

    • Impact**

I use Thunderbird extensively for professional correspondence and managing my translation business. These recurring freezes are seriously disrupting my workflow.

The problem has now persisted for over a month, despite updates and troubleshooting. It is becoming increasingly difficult to continue using Thunderbird in this condition.

    • What I would appreciate help investigating**

Could you please advise on how to identify the background process or operation that causes Thunderbird to become unresponsive after it has been running for several minutes?

In particular, I would appreciate guidance on:

- Whether this is a known regression affecting users who upgraded from much older Thunderbird versions. - Whether IMAP synchronization, background authentication, or Google OAuth activity could be responsible. - Whether there are diagnostic logs or performance profiles I can collect while Thunderbird is frozen. - Whether a particular database, profile component, or setting could be responsible without requiring me to rebuild my entire Thunderbird setup. - Whether there are known fixes or workarounds.

I'm happy to provide additional diagnostic information, screenshots, or logs if that would help identify the cause.

I would particularly appreciate a way to capture what Thunderbird is actually doing during these freezes, rather than continuing to try speculative troubleshooting steps.

Thank you in advance for your assistance!

title: Still want to see ALL messages sent my TB -- including spam / junk (the worst of the worst!)
creator: druw
content:
First off, mucho thanks to Wayne Mery for kindly guiding me back where I should again ask this question. Here's a copy of the message I posted that Wayne responded to --

> Hi Kelly, et al, > > If this isn't an appropriate place for my question / comment / suggestion -- please advise how to do it properly. > > Several months ago, I had a brief exchange with Wayne Merry(?) in which I communicated that I was "certain" that TB was not showing me ALL (99.99%) of the emails I receive for my several hosted domains. I mentioned that I used to receive 20-30-40 spam messages everyday -- mostly in "junk" (not all). Then suddenly that stopped -- perhaps after upgrading to a new version. Wayne seemed little interested in my problem, but suggested I upgrade to a newer version -- which I resisted (just want a "stable" version that works) -- but I did -- to 140.17 esr. > > That upgrade made little difference (maybe one or two more). That is very problematic for my "business-like" use of TB. I live by email. My business card minimizes my phone # (landline) and mainly shows two big, prominent e-addresses -- my old original e-address from an evil ISP in ATL (druw@oneimage.com)-- AND above that -- my main e-address which is identical to the ISP, but with DRU added to the domain (druw@OneImageDru.com). > > I verified this week that a banker business contact -- sent to both e-addresses -- and I only received the one sent to the ISP e-address. Never received the one sent to druw@OneImageDru.com -- at all. This is similar to dozens of similar situations -- in which I never received any (expected) email -- and had to assume that -- just maybe that party never sent an email (not a lot of email lovers left). > > How can I SEE ALL (99.99%) email sent to my TB -- including seeing ALL spam sent to my TB -- just verify that there aren't any unintended NON-spam messages that are being mischaracterized as spam -- but are not? Is there a particular TB version that has potentially solved this problem? > > Any suggestions for running an other particular IMAP client (not deleting) -- to compare with what I get with TB? > > Merci, > > Dru

Hello Dru. You were close with the name :)

Through https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/user/druw/ I see you previous posting No longer see ALL messages, including spam after upgrade to TB 128.14 Oesr (64, Win 10) from 6 months ago and your older posting More "granularity needed" to "How to turn off Junk filtering / TB 115.10 from a year ago.

The description of planning at https://thunderbird.topicbox.com/groups/planning/settings indicates this group is not for bug reporting and support. The place for support is https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/questions/new/thunderbird. You will want to state that the problem is seen with version 153 or newer, and in Troubleshoot Mode https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/troubleshoot-mode-thunderbird Thanks

Wayne
